One thing that has come up in discussion with @Tobias Rothmann regarding his work on hachi is that rewinding as it currently is in VCV will have to be tweaked. I recall from the early discussions on fiat-shamir that it it was also unsuited for this. Has the Fiat-Shamir work reached this point yet @Chung Thai Nguyen ?
Can we pre-agree to come up with a generic rewinding that each case can be an instance of and discuss this here / in the next arklib call?
It's not a 1:1 analogy but we could aim for something similar to the way I have done ring switching in https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/516 ?
@Alexander Hicks Do you mean rewinding soundness (which we are not prioritizing for now) or so? Or do you mean finding a common class interface for different ring-switching constructions?

In that case, from the DSFS side, we are not planning to work on rewinding soundness anytime soon, we are focusing on straight-line soundness & ZK.

For rewinding soundness there is a boilerplate in Rewinding.lean so Tobias can extend it if needed. I'm not sure what kind of soundness notions are used Hachi. If they are the ones in SNARGs book, the Fiat–Shamir transformations are ready to adopt them, together with the corresponding security transfer theorems.

Thanks for starting the discussion, Alex! 
So, for CWSS/Hachi, what we need is to analyze the tree of all possible query answers (or something related). So, in particular, a method to rewind a protocol run to a certain point, change one query, and then continue with the queries from before (i.e., change the query path only at one position). This seems kind of impossible with VCV-io’s current rewinding methods because 1. ForkReplay just samples everything new from the rewinding point on and 2. SeededOracle returns None for already-queried values.
@Chung Thai Nguyen I only see one definition and one structure in Rewinding.lean, is there more somewhere?

@Tobias Rothmann There is no more code on this. The current code let the extractor have access to prover as oracle. Maybe you can maintain a stack of messages up to the current round and the rewind action is simply popping the top messages, and when extractor wants to fork by throwing a new challenge we just push the new prover message into the stack. I'm not good at VCV-io so I can't give more ideas.
Quick message, (I'm on holiday). I believe we have this in SSProve and also in CatCrypt. The problem in EasyCrypt is that one doesn't have access to the syntax.

@Tobias Rothmann Are you saying that after changing the query you want to use the same responses to identical inputs as you did before rewinding, or you want to respond to things in the same order of responses (even if the adversary now gives different inputs)? I assume the former (for the coins these are the same since the input is always ())? I think either way I can get that by tweaking the current forking lemma stuff, although I'm not sure exactly what exact bounds they give should be, I think Jensen applies more easily when the continuation from forking is free.

Yes, I need to go back to a specific query, change that, get the new result for that query, and leave everything after that the same.
I'm not sure if a Jensen bound or something like that is general enough for what I want to prove, though, but maybe we can try that first.
If you're interested, you can see the concrete bounds I want to prove in Lemma 7.1 and 7.2 of this paper:
https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/846.pdf
